description: Switch a BUILD_ID variable from deferred (=) to immediate (:=) expansion, so every recipe line that references it during a single make run sees the SAME value instead of re-running the shell command each time
prompts: The Makefile defines `BUILD_ID = $(shell date +%s%N)` using `=` (recursively-expanded / deferred), which means $(shell ...) is re-invoked EVERY SINGLE TIME $(BUILD_ID) is referenced in a recipe - so the `stamp` target, which writes $(BUILD_ID) into build_id_a.txt and build_id_b.txt in two separate recipe lines, writes two DIFFERENT timestamps despite both lines running in the same `make` invocation. Fix it by changing `=` to `:=` (simply-expanded / immediate) so $(shell ...) runs ONCE when the Makefile is parsed, and every reference to $(BUILD_ID) afterward - across the whole `make` run - sees that same value.

setup_files.Makefile:
BUILD_ID = $(shell date +%s%N)

.PHONY: stamp
stamp:
	echo $(BUILD_ID) > build_id_a.txt
	echo $(BUILD_ID) > build_id_b.txt

test_setup_files.test_build_id.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

r = subprocess.run(['make', 'stamp'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'make stamp failed: {r.stderr}'

a = Path('build_id_a.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip()
b = Path('build_id_b.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip()
assert a == b, (
    f'BUILD_ID differs between the two recipe lines within the SAME make run '
    f'(a={a!r}, b={b!r}) - $(shell ...) is being re-run on every reference, which means '
    f'BUILD_ID is still deferred (=) instead of immediate (:=)')

print('PASS')
